Custom alias and expiry date

**99.99%** availability

QR codes

blocks.title: TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Reads are 100x writes: size the redirect path for 12,000/s peak, p99 under 50 ms.

items: Click events go ==async== to Kafka, **never** on the critical path
Kafka down? Redirects work, counts lag

blocks.title: DESIGN TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Split reads, keep clicks async, pick 302.

items: Create, resolve, inspect, delete links
==Auth== via API key on management endpoints
==Idempotency==: retried POSTs mint one code
Redirect path: one lookup, one header

blocks.note: Same key retried returns same code

items: Create ==p99 under 200 ms==
Redirect ==p99 under 50 ms==
4xx/5xx rates **per endpoint**
==Counter==: no collisions, **guessable**
==Hash==: first 7 of MD5/SHA; retry on collision
==Snowflake== 64-bit: no counter, **11 chars**
6B links in 5 years: 7 chars, 40 writes/s

blocks.note: XOR key also works; keep it secret

items: Truncated hash, no check: two URLs, one code
Same URL, one code: breaks per-user links
Hash collision: insert fails, retry with salt
ID service down: leased range covers ~25 s

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Range lease plus bijective shuffle: no collisions, no sequential codes. Alert: retries >0.1% or <100 IDs left.

items: ==code== to `long_url`, **4,000** reads/s
~40 writes/s, no contention
3 TB over 5 years, sharded
~500 B/row: 3 TB in 5 years, so shard
`hash(code)`: 16 shards x ==~200 GB==
Pure key lookup: ==KV store== (DynamoDB, Cassandra)
SQL: transactions, unique keys. NoSQL: easy scale
`user_id` index serves 'my links', off hot path
RF 3, quorum reads: one node can die
Viral hot code: cache absorbs it
Index lag delays 'my links', never redirects
Click counters in links row: write contention
Count clicks in analytics store
Quorum read p99 under 10 ms
Shard size alert at 160 GB (80%)
Cache hit above 95%, DB ~200 reads/s
Cache-aside, ==TTL 24 h==; LRU evicts coldest codes
35 GB hot set, **95%** hits: DB ~200 reads/s
Negative cache, unknown codes, **60 s**: blocks scans
CDN caches 301s for static hot links, clicks lost
Delete or expiry change: cache delete; TTL bounds staleness
Edge cache hit: answer, no origin trip
Redis `GET code`: hit returns long URL
Miss: read DB, `SET` with TTL
Unknown code: 60 s negative entry, 404
Reply **302** with `Location`

blocks.note: one DB read per key, jittered TTL

items: Viral stampede: single-flight merges misses, one DB read
Jittered TTL (24 h + up to 1 h) avoids synchronized expiry
Random-code scans: 60 s negative cache shields DB
Deleted link cached: `DEL code`, TTL caps staleness 24 h
CDN 301 hides repeat clicks: static hot links only
Cache hit rate over **95%**
Redirect p99 under **50 ms**
DB read QPS, ~200/s
Cache memory, hot set ~35 GB

blocks.title: TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Hit rate is the lever: 95% turns 4,000/s into ~200 DB reads/s.

items: Count clicks; capture ==referrer==, country, device without slowing redirects
Redirect service publishes a click to {icon:apachekafka} **Kafka**, fire-and-forget
About 4,000 events/s x 300 B is about ==100 GB/day== raw
Flink aggregates per code per minute into ClickHouse
Raw events kept 30 days; roll-ups kept **2 years**
Kafka down: buffer locally, ==drop clicks== rather than fail redirects
Retries duplicate events; dedupe on `event_id` keeps counts consistent
Consumer lag under **30 s**
Track drop rate; event loss under **0.1%**
==Alias== 3-30 chars, `[a-zA-Z0-9-]`
Reserved (`api`, `admin`, `login`) **blocked**
Taken alias: PK conditional insert, **409**
Shares namespace with generated codes
Store `expires_at`; later reads **410 Gone**
Two claim `promo`: PK admits one, 409 other
Alias equals generated code: reserve space
Expired row lingers: lazy delete, sweeper
Cache outlives expiry: TTL `min(24 h, expiry)`
**Mistake**: recycling expired codes opens old URLs

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: PK decides uniqueness; check expiry on read; retire codes forever.

items: Creates: ==100/hour== per API key, anonymous ==10/hour== per IP
Redirects capped near **100/s** per IP at the edge
Scan targets with Safe Browsing at create, re-scan nightly
Block-list bad domains; reject loops and shortener self-links
Disable a flagged link in under **1 minute**, cache purged

blocks.title: TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Limit the cheap write, scan the target, and fail open so a Redis outage never stops redirects.

items: Stateless app tier behind ==LB==
{icon:redis} Redis split by **consistent hashing**
DB shards `hash(code)`: 16 x ~200 GB
==Active-active reads== via geo-DNS
Writes to **home region**, async replication

blocks.text: Why 20x: 95% hits leave DB ~200 reads/s; Redis gone, all **4,000/s**. 1,000 IDs last ~**25 s** at 40 writes/s.

items: Geo-DNS sends each reader to the ==nearest region==
Writes route to the **home region** of the owner
Async replication: a new link may 404 briefly elsewhere
Region down: geo-DNS reroutes reads to the next closest
Kafka down: buffer locally, ==drop clicks==
Limiter store down: **fail open**, local cap
Shard down: replica reads, quorum holds
Redirects stay up; analytics and creates lag first

blocks.title: Shed load in order
blocks.text: Scans first, then creates, never redirects.

items: Skipping the ID prefetch: ID outage stops creates
Retrying Redis misses blindly: DB meltdown

blocks.title: Redis outage tip
blocks.text: DB takes ~20x load, so rate-limit and shed scans first.

blocks.q: Q1. How do you avoid collisions across servers?
Q2. How do you handle a viral link?
a_bullets: Replicate hot key across Redis nodes

caption.text:
"How would you design a URL shortener for millions of users?"

This is a classic system design interview question, and it's easy to ramble on. Here's the bit.ly-style design, about 40 writes/s and 4,000 redirects/s on average, as handwritten notes.

What's inside, in order:

1. Problem, requirements and scale estimates
2. High-level architecture
3. API design
4. Short-code generation: base62, counters, hashing
5. Data model and storage
6. Redirect path and caching
7. Analytics pipeline
8. Custom aliases and expiry
9. Rate limiting and abuse prevention
10. Scaling, failure handling and interview questions

Save this for your next system design round and share it with a friend who's prepping.
